title: Employee Free Time
description: Brute force to optimized: marking every individual time unit versus flattening all schedules and applying standard Merge Intervals to find the gaps.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given the working schedule for a company's employees, where schedule[i] is a sorted list of non-overlapping intervals representing employee i's working time, return a sorted list of finite intervals representing the COMMON, positive-length free time shared by ALL employees, ignoring the open ends of the overall timeline (before the first interval and after the last).

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.text: The company is collectively busy during any time covered by AT LEAST ONE employee's schedule. This means combining every employee's intervals into a single list and merging overlaps gives the exact busy periods for the WHOLE company; any gap between these merged busy periods is, by definition, free time for every employee simultaneously.

blocks.title: Analogy: Finding a Meeting Time That Works for an Entire Team
blocks.text: Picture wanting to find a time slot when NOBODY on a team is busy, given each person's individual meeting schedule. Combining every person's busy times into one big list, merging any that overlap, reveals the entire team's collective busy periods; whatever time is left between them is when everyone is simultaneously free.

blocks.caption: Flatten every employee's intervals into one list, merge overlaps, and the gaps are the shared free time

blocks.text: Result: [[3,4]]. Combined busy intervals merge into [1,3] and [4,10] (and [1,2],[5,6] merge in since they fall within these); the gap between them, [3,4], is the only common free time.

Before tracking each employee's schedule separately and cross-referencing them, notice that "free for everyone" is exactly the complement of "busy for at least one employee," which means combining ALL employees' intervals into one list and applying standard interval merging directly gives the company-wide busy periods, whose gaps are the answer.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: The company as a whole is busy at any moment covered by ANY employee's working interval, regardless of which employee.

Observation 2: This means the distinction between employees can be discarded entirely once the goal shifts to finding company-wide busy periods; combining every interval from every employee into one flat list is valid.

Observation 3: Sorting this combined list by start time and merging overlapping intervals (the standard Merge Intervals technique) produces the exact set of company-wide busy periods.

Observation 4: The GAPS between these consecutive merged busy periods are, by definition, moments when NO employee is working, i.e., common free time for everyone.

This leads to flattening every employee's intervals into one combined list, sorting and merging them via standard Merge Intervals, then reporting the gaps between consecutive merged intervals as the answer.
Check every possible unit of time within the overall range, determining whether it falls within any employee's working interval, and collecting the maximal stretches where none do.

items: Determine the overall time range spanning all schedules.
For each unit of time in this range, check whether it falls within ANY employee's working interval.
Collect maximal stretches where no employee is working as free time intervals.

codes.python:
def employee_free_time_brute(schedule):
    all_intervals = [iv for emp in schedule for iv in emp]
    lo = min(iv[0] for iv in all_intervals)
    hi = max(iv[1] for iv in all_intervals)
    busy = [False] * (hi - lo + 1)
    for start, end in all_intervals:
        for t in range(start, end):                       # mark every busy unit directly
            busy[t - lo] = True
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(busy):
        if not busy[i]:
            j = i
            while j < len(busy) and not busy[j]:
                j += 1
            if i > 0 and j < len(busy):                       # only interior gaps count
                result.append([lo + i, lo + j])
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return result

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Marking every individual time unit directly and correctly identifies busy versus free time.
This costs time proportional to the TOTAL TIME RANGE spanned, which can be vastly larger than the actual number of intervals involved.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(total time range spanned), potentially far larger than the interval count.
Space: O(total time range spanned).

Limitation: working directly with intervals (via sort and merge) rather than individual time units reduces the cost to O(N log N), N being the total number of intervals across all employees, independent of the time range's magnitude.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why working at the level of individual time units is wasteful: the actual number of INTERVALS is what matters, not the magnitude of the time values themselves, which could span a huge range with relatively few actual intervals.

The flatten-and-merge approach: combine all N intervals across every employee into one list; sort by start time; merge overlapping intervals exactly as in standard Merge Intervals, in O(N log N).

Extracting the answer: after merging, walk through the merged list once, and for every pair of CONSECUTIVE merged intervals, the gap between the first one's end and the second one's start is a valid piece of common free time.

The core idea: treat "company-wide free time" as literally the Merge Intervals problem applied to the union of all employees' schedules, then read off the gaps.

Flatten all employees' intervals into one list. Sort by start time and merge overlaps (standard Merge Intervals). Walk through the merged list once, recording the gap between each pair of consecutive merged intervals as a free time interval.

Any gap between two consecutive merged busy periods is, by construction, a stretch of time no employee is working, which is exactly the definition of common free time.

blocks.text: Employee Free Time is an elegant demonstration that "common free time across multiple schedules" reduces directly to the standard Merge Intervals problem, once the distinction between individual employees is dropped in favor of company-wide busy periods.

items: Trying to track each employee's schedule separately and cross-reference them, missing the simpler flatten-and-merge reduction.
Forgetting that the answer only includes INTERIOR gaps (between merged intervals), not the open-ended time before the first or after the last.

blocks.text: Explicitly stating "this reduces to Merge Intervals on the flattened, employee-agnostic list of all busy times" is the key insight that should be stated clearly before coding.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "find time free across MULTIPLE independent schedules", think: flatten all schedules into one list, merge overlaps, and read off the gaps.

items: How would you find free time for only a SUBSET of employees, not all of them?
How would you handle schedules that update dynamically over time, without re-merging everything from scratch?
Merge Intervals, the exact core technique this problem reduces to after flattening.
Any "find gaps in combined coverage from multiple independent sources" problem.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: Marking individual time units costs time proportional to the total time range, potentially far larger than needed; the flatten-sort-merge approach costs O(N log N) time and O(N) space, independent of the time range's magnitude.

items: Pattern: reduce "common free time across multiple schedules" to standard Merge Intervals on the flattened, combined list.
Core Idea: flatten all employees' intervals into one list, sort and merge overlaps, then report the gaps between consecutive merged intervals.
Time: O(total time range) for the brute force, O(N log N) for the optimized flatten-and-merge approach.
Most Important Observation: "free for everyone" is exactly the gaps in the union of everyone's busy time, reducing this multi-schedule problem to a single Merge Intervals call.
Interview Difficulty: an elegant reduction problem, testing recognition that employee identity is irrelevant once busy time is combined.
One line memory trick: flatten all schedules, merge intervals, report the gaps.
